title: Bridging the Urban-Rural Divide in Dyslexia Intervention: Evaluating the Regional Heterogeneous Impact of the DRSSI Model Under National and Rivers State Inclusive Education Policies
content: Children with dyslexia across urban and rural regions in Nigeria continue to face barriers to equitable education. This situation is particularly evident when urban–rural disparities affect teacher capacity, resources, and access to appropriate supports. This paper presents the Dyslexia-Responsive Schools System Initiative (DRSSI) as a school-system model designed to bridge the gap in inclusive education policy and implementation in Rivers State, Nigeria. To achieve this, the DRSSI model integrates six interconnected components to create dyslexia-friendly school system. The paper argues that prevailing monolithic implementation approaches may inadequately address the differing realities of urban and rural schools due to regional heterogeneity (RH) as a contextual determinant. The paper proposes the SAFE framework (Scalability, Adaptability, Feasibility, and Effectiveness) for critically evaluating the intended outcomes of the DRSSI’s implementation. Aspects of the DRSSI model that require further development were discussed. The paper recommends policy guidelines to the Rivers State education authorities that are regionally responsive, local stakeholder engagement, and equity-weighted resource allocation to strengthen implementation across schools and local government areas. The paper positions DRSSI as a potential model for advancing equitable, context-responsive dyslexia-friendly schools, while emphasising the need for systematic evaluation before its effectiveness and wider scalability can be established.
